Hi @ed@tanous.net, @molberding@nvidia.com,

This is the non-coroutine, callback-based deferrd_reply API I proposed in 89528 (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/89528).

Could you take a look and let me know whether the direction and scoping match what you had in mind? 

Thanks!
Suggestion: clarify that subsequent send/send_errno/send_error calls are silently ignored.

Done.
Statement added to clarify the case of silently ignored if having duplicated functon calls.

Only argument count is checked, not types.
Suggest adding:
```
  static_assert((std::is_convertible_v<Args&&, ReturnTypes> && ...),
                "deferred_reply::send argument types must be "
                "convertible to ReturnTypes");
```

Done.
Types checking is added accordingly!

replied_ is set before the reply is actually sent. If append() / method_return() throws, replied_ stays true and the destructor skips the auto-EIO fallback → caller times out.
Suggest moving the assignment after method_return() succeeds, or wrap in try/catch like coroutine_method_instance::after_spawn.

Done.
The assignment of `replied_ = true` moved to the line after `.method_return()`

send_errno(int error) doesn't document whether 'error' should be passed as positive or negative. Because the doc example and abandon path use -EIO, coroutine_method_instance at Line 267 passes the positive e.get_errno(). 
Suggest a brief doxygen note on send_errno clarifying the expected sign.

Done.
Added a doxygen error block on `send_errno()`.
Same problem as Line 357.

Done.
Moved to the line after `err.method_return();`
Same problem as Line 357.

Done.
Moved to the line after `err.method_return()`
Suggestion: add a brief comment like line 241, e.g. "make a copy of m to move into the deferred reply".

Done.
Added a comment stating how `message_t{m}` is passed into the function.
LGTM
why does the move assignment operator call abandon_if_unreplied but the move construction operator doesn't? These should generally symmetric.

The asymmetry is intentional. In move-construction `*this` is being created and `request_` is directly initialized from `other.request_` in the mem-init list. So there is no prior request on `*this` to abandon.
However, in the move-assignment, `*this` already exists and may hold a live un-replied request. Calling `abandon_if_unreplied()` first sends `-EIO` to that original caller before we overwrite(otherwise they will time out).
Is it safe to call this twice?

I think yes because `abandon_if_unreplied()` is idempotent.
It guards on `if (replied_ || ~request_) return;` initially and set `replied_ = true` at the end, so any second call will be short-circuited at the guard.
nit: this statement contradicts itself. Sounds like what you are trying to describe is idempotency?

Thanks for the catching!
Rewrote the statement.
Please add something to asio_example that tests this and shows its use.

Thanks for acknowledging.
I have added example in `example/deferred-method-example.cpp` to demonstrate how it can be used.

1.  Please correct this to use the asio convention. This would be called a "completion"
2. Please put this kind of documentation in the documentation and examples, not inline.
3. Please remove internal error codes.  Describe the public API.

Done. 
1. Migrated implementation to `sdbusplus::asio::completion`, and the API is now called `register_completion_method`.
2. Noted and already moved the documentation to `docs/asio.md`.
3. Noted. Expose only `send()` now and have described the API in the document.

Still seeing issues here.  Completions generally do not have a "send" method, which would prevent chaining (ie, passing an sdbusplus completion to an asio callback and vice versa).

https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/doc/html/boost_asio/overview/model/completion_tokens.html

Can you please read, and ack that you've read and understand that.  Once that's done, we can start looking at individual issues.

I've read the completion-token overview you linked and understand that an async operation should take a completion token as its final argument so the same operation composes across callbacks, futures, coroutines, ..., etc.

In this revision, I took that to its conclusion and removed the abstraction altogether. There is no completion/handle type and no `send()`. Instead, I added a `deferred` flag that only suppresses the automatic reply, and the handler keeps the call `message_t` and replies through the normal message API (`new_method_return()` / `new_method_errno()`).

The consequence is that there is no new async primitive to fit into the completion-token model. However, if you'd still prefer the completion-token-based reply type, I'm glad to take it that direction.

The latest patch I pushed is just to propose the minimal form that adds no public type and reuses the existing path.

> I took that to its conclusion and removed the abstraction altogether.

This is not what I asked for.  I asked you to keep the completion, and make it compliant with asio completion tokens.

> if you'd still prefer the completion-token-based reply type, I'm glad to take it that direction.

Yes, this is what I prefer.  This is so that chaining of callbacks works properly with normal asio sockets/queues/events.

Apologize for the misunderstanding. I have reworked and done in the way you asked. The completion approach is kept and made asio-compliant.

In this revision, `sdbusplus::asio::completion<Results...>` lives in its own file (`completion.hpp`) and has no `send()` nethod, and exposes only `operator()(boost::system::error_code, Results...)`.
I think it should be a proper asio completion handler now and is able to chains with normal asio callbacks.

The inline documentation is also moved to `docs/asio.md` now.
put this in its own file please.
Done. `completion` and `completion_method_instance` now live in `include/sdbusplus/asio/completion.hpp`.
?  Why are we abandoning on a move?
Removed, with the destructor reply gone there is nothing to abandon, and the constructor and assignment operation()= are now symmetric.
are we sure we want to be sending a reply on a destructor?

The intention was to catch if the consumer has any unsend reply.
However, that seems to be redundant as completing the call is explicitly the handler's responsibility.
In this case, I have removed this in the latest implementation.
Thanks for acknowledging!

> the call is explicitly the handler's

Also timeouts are already handled internally by dbus.  No need to try to do anything clever here.
Remove these.  They duplicate behavior on sdbusplus::message

Done. 
Removed the 2 redundant error handling functions.
Surely you don't want to catch all exceptions?   Presumably you only want to catch sd-bus messages.

Done.
This cases is no longer needed anymore as we have abandoned the consumer of this function.
Why are we needing template expansion here?  I suspect we need to just invent some new methods and avoid needing to detect template types.
Done. Discarded this implementation in the latest patch.
A lot of this looks duplicated with register_method.  Is there any ways to avoid the duplication?

Done.
Factored the shared registration logic into a private helper `addMethodCallback()`.
Why are we making a copy?  We spent quite a bit of time trying to make the existing methods not copy.

Done.
Switched to `std::move()` to transfer the ownership.

I'm a little confused how this works....  If you're registering this in the normal table, isn't it just doing a blocking call still?

When you write your example, maybe include a timer in the callback to show that it's working the way we expect it to.

It is not blocking.
The dispatch handler `completion_method_instance::operator()` returns 1 without calling `method_return()`; 
so the dispatch is released immediately and the reply is transmitted later from `completion::send()` on whatever callback completes the work. 
This is the same mechanism the coroutine path already uses, and the completion path just swaps the coroutine for a caller-owned completion.
You've only added one method, please just add an example of this call to the existing asio example rather than rewriting the whole thing.
Done. The standalone `completion-method-example.cpp` is dropped, and a single deferred method is added to the existing `example/asio-exmaple.cpp`.
asio completion objects generally don't take arbitrary arguments.  Do we need to be explicit here, and template this based on the return types in the regisetered function?

I have removed the completion object, so there is no longer a type taking arbitrary arguments.
On the underlying return-type question, a deferred handler returns `void` and sends its reply through `message_t`, so the method's declared output signature is currently empty.

This should be in a separate patch.  I like the idea of having this, but some level of description for what it does and why (in the commit message) is required, and a separate patchset is the best way to do that.

Understood, I have splitted the example implementation into another patch. Please find them in the following link:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/sdbusplus/+/91295
Sorry, there appears to be a misunderstanding here.  the example should go in this patch, or in its own stadalone patch.  the "startHeartbeat" feature should go in a different patch.
Please condense.

Done in the separated patchset.
The inline narration is removed and the handler contract is documented in `docs/asio.md` instead.

This is still not how asio would handle completions.  You were closer on your last patch.  There should be a callable (token) passed to the method, that on completion can be called with either an error or a success, and the arguments that get returned.

Thanks for acknowledging. 
I have reworked and the handler can now receives and `sdbusplus::asio::completion` as its last argument instead of a raw `message_t`.
Please keep this in line with the lambda rules.  This likely needs to be a method.

Done.
The asynchronous work is now moved out of the registration into a named function, `completeDeferredCall()`.

Please don't continue overloading the register_method.  If you want to keep common code, make a common private method that both public methods can call, but we're already overloading this callback a lot more than I'd like to see with the various variations of msg/types/flags, and now defered.  Lets just make a new method like you had on patchset 1.

Done.
`register_method()` is now reverted and the deferred path is now a separate `register_completion_method()`, as on PS1, and the common vtable registration is factored into a private `addMethodCallback()` that both methods call.
Shouldn't this be accepted by rvalue (ie &&)

Done.
The handler is now taking the completion by rvalue reference.
error codes should be taken by const reference.

Done.
I have modified the example and the related function is now taking `const` argument for error code.

Double tiered lambda calls are definitely outside of what's allowed in the coding standard.  Lets make sure our examples comply with the coding best practices.

Also, if this example could be made to use bind_front, it would be much cleaner.

Done. 
I have removed the nested lambda and explicitly declared the involved functions so that we can use the `std::bind_front` approach to link them together.
Please follow the appropriate naming conventions throughout this patch.

Done.
I have aligned the naming to the snake_case instead of camelCase.

Sorry, not understanding why this needs to exist.  Can't completion just have a

using result_type = std::tuple<Results...>;

Rather than inventing a whole new traits?


This looks very similar to some of the other meta helper classes that exist already, can this be combined?

Done.
I have moved `result_type = std::tuple<Results...>` into the class itself.

Lets not allow flags to be set on this for now.  exposing sd-bus externals in register_method wasn't the best idea in the first place, so lets not continue to propagate it.  The majority of calls set no flags, so this should be fine.

This also keeps CallbackType as the last parameter, in line with how asio models these.
and if we want to support flags later, lets discuss that in the next patch.

Understood.
Dropped `flags` from `register_completion_method()` in PS 13.
I think we don't necessarily need them now.

Sorry, what is a dispatcher?  Is suspect this comment needs some rework.

"shared tail" i'm not sure about either.
Reworded. The comment is now stating plainly that the helper records one method in the vtable and is called by both `register_method()` and `register_completion_method()`.
